title: What is dhikr? (Dhikr)
text:
Dhikr means remembrance. It is saying short phrases that remember Allah, like SubhanAllah (Glory be to Allah), Alhamdulillah (All praise is for Allah) and Allahu Akbar (Allah is the Greatest). People say them quietly, many times over, at any time of day.
The Quran says: “Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah hearts are assured” (13:28), and tells believers to “remember Allah with much remembrance” (33:41). The Prophet ﷺ described two phrases as light on the tongue, heavy on the scales and loved by the Most Merciful: SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi, SubhanAllahil-ʿAzeem (Sahih al-Bukhari 6682). Many Muslims find it calms the mind and keeps Allah close through an ordinary day.
You can count on your fingers or on prayer beads, which are also called a tasbeeh. A well-known set after each prayer is SubhanAllah 33 times, Alhamdulillah 33 times and Allahu Akbar 34 times (Sahih Muslim 596). There is no special place or time needed: walking, waiting or before sleep are all good moments.
src: Quran 13:28; Quran 33:41; Sahih al-Bukhari 6682; Sahih Muslim 596

title: What is salah? (Salah)
text:
Salah is the prayer Muslims perform five times a day: standing, bowing, prostrating and sitting, while reciting the Quran in Arabic. It is the second of the five pillars of Islam.
Allah says: “Establish prayer for My remembrance” (20:14), and “Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing” (29:45). Five times a day it pauses whatever you are doing and turns you back to Allah.
The five prayers are Fajr (before sunrise), Dhuhr (after midday), Asr (afternoon), Maghrib (just after sunset) and Isha (night). Each has its own window of time, and Munib shows when each begins. If you are learning, your local mosque or a teacher can show you how to pray step by step.

title: Why do prayer times change, and why do apps differ? (Prayer times)
text:
The prayer times follow the sun, not the clock. Fajr begins with the first light of dawn, Dhuhr just after the sun passes its highest point, Asr in the afternoon as shadows lengthen, Maghrib at sunset and Isha when the sky is fully dark. So the times shift a little every day.
Allah says: “Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times” (4:103).
Fajr and Isha depend on how dark the sky is, and Muslim organisations measure that in slightly different ways, which is why apps and mosques can differ by a few minutes (in the UK summer, by more). For Asr, most schools start it when a shadow equals an object’s length, and the Hanafi school when it is twice the length. You can choose both under Prayer times and alerts. If you are unsure, follow your local mosque.

title: What is the Qibla? (Qibla)
text:
The Qibla is the direction of the Kaaba, the cube-shaped house of worship at the centre of the Grand Mosque in Makkah. Muslims everywhere face it when they pray, so the whole ummah turns towards one place.
Allah says: “So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram. And wherever you [believers] are, turn your faces toward it” (2:144). The Quran tells how Ibrahim and his son Ismail raised its foundations (2:127).
Hold your phone flat and turn until Munib says you are facing the Qibla. Many scholars say that when you are far from Makkah, facing the general direction is enough, so do your best and don’t worry about a degree or two.

title: What is jamaʿah? (Jamaʿah)
text:
Jamaʿah means praying together, in rows, following an imam who leads the prayer. Each mosque sets its own jamaʿah time, usually a little after the prayer begins, so people can gather.
The Prophet ﷺ said prayer in congregation is twenty-seven times better than praying alone (Sahih al-Bukhari 645). It is also where many people meet their community.
Add your mosque in Munib to see its jamaʿah times and get an alert before each one. If it is your first visit, it is fine to tell someone you are new: people are usually glad to help.

title: What is Jumuʿah? (Jumuʿah)
text:
Jumuʿah is the Friday congregational prayer. It takes the place of Dhuhr on Fridays and begins with a sermon, the khutbah. Busy mosques often hold it more than once (a 1st and 2nd Jumuʿah).
Allah says: “O you who have believed, when [the adhan] is called for the prayer on the day of Jumuʿah, then proceed to the remembrance of Allah and leave trade” (62:9).
Arrive a little early if you can. Many Muslims also read Surah al-Kahf on Fridays.

title: What is dua? (Dua)
text:
Dua is asking Allah directly for what you need: help, forgiveness, healing, guidance, anything. It can be in your own words and in any language, at any time. There are also duas with words taught in the Quran and by the Prophet ﷺ, which Munib collects for different moments.
Allah says: “And when My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me” (2:186), and “Call upon Me; I will respond to you” (40:60).
Many people raise their hands, begin by praising Allah and sending blessings on the Prophet ﷺ, then ask. Keep asking, and trust that Allah answers in the way that is best.

title: Why pray for other people? (Dua for others)
text:
Muslims are encouraged to pray for each other, especially quietly, when the other person doesn’t know. Ask for dua lets you share what you are going through and let others pray for you.
The Prophet ﷺ said that when a Muslim prays for his brother in his absence, an angel says: “And for you the same” (Sahih Muslim 2733).
Read a request, make a short dua for that person in your own words, then tap “I made dua” so they know someone prayed. Nobody sees who made dua for them.

title: What are adhkar? (Adhkar)
text:
Adhkar (the plural of dhikr) are set words of remembrance for particular moments: waking up, leaving home, eating, sleeping, and the morning and evening adhkar. The best-known collection is Hisn al-Muslim, “The Fortress of the Muslim”, which Munib’s duas come from.
Saying them ties the ordinary parts of the day back to Allah, following words the Prophet ﷺ himself used.
Start with one or two that fit your day, such as the dua before sleep, and add more as they become a habit.

title: What is a khatm? (Khatm)
text:
A khatm is a complete reading of the Quran, from the first surah to the last. Families and friends often share one out, each person taking a juz (one of 30 parts), so together they finish it, for example in Ramadan or after someone passes away.
The Quran is the word of Allah, and reading it is worship in itself. The Prophet ﷺ said the best of people are those who learn the Quran and teach it (Sahih al-Bukhari 5027).
Start a khatm, invite people with the link, and everyone picks a juz. Munib keeps track of who is reading what and how far each person has got.

title: Can we read for someone who has died? (Reading for someone who passed)
text:
When someone dies, many families gather to read the Quran together and make dua for them. Munib lets you start a khatm in their name, with a dua for the deceased.
Scholars agree that dua for someone who has died reaches them. The Prophet ﷺ said that when a person dies their deeds end, except three, one of which is a righteous child who prays for them (Sahih Muslim 1631). Whether the reward of reading the Quran itself reaches them is something scholars discuss, so ask your imam if you want to know more.
Make dua for them by name whenever you finish your juz.

title: What is a juz? (Juz)
text:
The Quran is divided into 30 parts of roughly equal length, each called a juz (plural ajzaʾ). They make it easy to read a set amount, and reading one a day finishes the whole Quran in a month, which many people aim for in Ramadan.
A juz is about 20 pages of a printed Quran. Even a few pages a day finishes it in a year or two.

title: What are surahs and ayat? (Surah and ayah)
text:
The Quran has 114 surahs, or chapters, from very long ones like al-Baqarah to short ones of three ayat. Each surah is made of ayat (singular ayah), usually translated as verses. Ayah also means “sign”: each one is a sign from Allah.
A reference like 2:255 means surah 2, ayah 255.

title: Why learn surahs by heart? (Surahs for your prayer)
text:
In every unit of the prayer you recite al-Fatihah, the Quran’s opening surah, from memory, and in the first two units most people add a short surah after it. Learning a handful of short surahs lets you vary what you recite and understand it better.
The Prophet ﷺ said the best of people are those who learn the Quran and teach it (Sahih al-Bukhari 5027). Many new Muslims start with al-Fatihah and al-Ikhlas.
Learn one ayah at a time: listen, repeat, then test yourself. A teacher at your local mosque can check your pronunciation.

title: What is tafsir? (Tafsir)
text:
Tafsir is the explanation of the Quran: what an ayah means, when and why it was revealed, and how the Prophet ﷺ and his companions understood it. Munib uses the Tafsir of Ibn Kathir, a 14th-century scholar from Damascus, one of the most widely read.
Tap Tafsir on any ayah. A translation gives the words; a tafsir gives the context.

title: What is a mushaf? (Mushaf)
text:
A mushaf is a written or printed copy of the Quran. Munib’s page view shows the Madani Mushaf, printed in Madinah and used in mosques around the world, with the same 604 pages, so “page 50” means the same thing to everyone using it.
It reads from right to left, so swipe right to turn the page.

title: What is the ummah? (Ummah)
text:
The ummah is the whole community of Muslims around the world, across every country, language and background.
The Prophet ﷺ said the believers, in their love and mercy for one another, are like one body: when one part hurts, the whole body feels it (Sahih al-Bukhari 6011).
Praying for each other, reading together and helping each other are all part of being one ummah.

title: Why is the last third of the night special? (The last third of the night)
text:
The night, from Maghrib to Fajr, can be split into three. The last third, before dawn, is a time Muslims try to wake for prayer and dua.
The Prophet ﷺ said that in the last third of every night, Allah says: “Who is calling upon Me, that I may answer him? Who is asking of Me, that I may give him? Who is seeking My forgiveness, that I may forgive him?” (Sahih al-Bukhari 1145).
Prayer times shows when the last third begins tonight. Even a few minutes of dua before Fajr counts.

title: Prayer step: Stand and intend (Niyyah)
text:
Stand facing the Qibla, feet a little apart, and look down at the place where your forehead will go. In your heart, intend the prayer you are about to pray, for example “the two rakʿahs of Fajr”. The intention is in the heart; you don’t need special words.
Done differently: Some scholars say the intention quietly in words as well; most say the heart is enough. Ask your local imam what they teach.

title: Prayer step: Raise your hands and begin (Takbir)
text:
Raise your hands to the level of your ears or shoulders, palms facing forward, and say “Allahu akbar”. From now on you are in prayer: stay still, keep your eyes on your place of prostration, and don’t talk.
Say: Allahu akbar — "Allah is the Greatest." [Said at each change of position]
src: Said at each change of position

title: Prayer step: Fold your hands and open the prayer (Qiyam)
text:
Place your right hand over your left. Quietly say the opening words of praise. They are recommended, so if you don’t know them yet, your prayer is still fine without them.
Say: Subhanakal-lahumma wabihamdika watabarakas-muka wataʿala jadduka wala ilaha ghayruk. — "How perfect You are O Allah, and I praise You. Blessed be Your name, and lofty is Your position, and none has the right to be worshipped except You." [Hisn al-Muslim, no. 28]
Done differently: Where the hands go differs: on the chest, just below it, or below the navel; many Malikis let their arms hang by their sides. All of these are followed by Muslims, so do what your local mosque teaches.

title: Prayer step: Seek refuge with Allah (Taʿawwudh)
text:
Before you recite, quietly seek refuge with Allah from Satan. Al-Fatihah then begins in His name: “Bismillahir-rahmanir-raheem”.
Say: Aʿoodhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajeem — "I seek refuge with Allah from Satan, the outcast." [Based on Quran 16:98]

title: Prayer step: Recite al-Fatihah (Al-Fatihah)
text:
Recite al-Fatihah, the opening surah, in every rakʿah. It is the heart of the prayer, so it is the first thing to learn. At the end, say “Ameen”.
Say: Ameen — "O Allah, answer us." [Said after al-Fatihah]
Done differently: In Fajr, Maghrib and Isha the first two rakʿahs are recited aloud by the imam; Dhuhr and Asr are quiet. When you pray behind an imam, schools differ on whether you recite al-Fatihah yourself. Ask your local imam.

title: Prayer step: Recite a short surah (Surah)
text: In the first two rakʿahs, after al-Fatihah, recite any other part of the Quran you know: a short surah is perfect. Al-Ikhlas is a good one to start with. In the third and fourth rakʿahs you recite al-Fatihah only.

title: Prayer step: Bow (Rukuʿ)
text:
Say “Allahu akbar” and bow, with your hands on your knees and your back straight and level. Pause until you are still, and glorify your Lord.
Say: Allahu akbar — "Allah is the Greatest." [Said at each change of position]
Say: Subhana rabbiyal-ʿatheem — "How perfect my Lord is, the Supreme." (3 times) [Hisn al-Muslim, no. 33]
src: Said at each change of position; Hisn al-Muslim, no. 33

title: Prayer step: Rise and stand still (Iʿtidal)
text:
Rise back up to standing, saying the first words as you rise. Stand fully straight and still for a moment, then praise Allah.
Say: Samiʿal-lahu liman hamidah — "Allah hears the one who praises Him." [Hisn al-Muslim, no. 38 (said while rising)]
Say: Rabbana walakal-hamdu hamdan katheeran tayyiban mubarakan feeh. — "Our Lord, for You is all praise, an abundant, beautiful, blessed praise." [Hisn al-Muslim, no. 39]
Done differently: Behind an imam, many schools teach that you say only “Rabbana walakal-hamd” while the imam says “Samiʿallahu liman hamidah”.
src: Hisn al-Muslim, no. 38 (said while rising); Hisn al-Muslim, no. 39

title: Prayer step: Prostrate (Sujud)
text:
Say “Allahu akbar” and go down into prostration. Seven parts touch the ground: your forehead (with your nose), both palms, both knees and the toes of both feet. Keep your forearms off the ground. This is when you are closest to Allah.
Say: Allahu akbar — "Allah is the Greatest." [Said at each change of position]
Say: Subhana rabbiyal-aʿla — "How perfect my Lord is, the Most High." (3 times) [Hisn al-Muslim, no. 41]
Done differently: Whether the knees or the hands touch the ground first, and how far the elbows are held from the body, differ between schools (many teach women to keep their arms closer in). Ask your local imam.
src: Said at each change of position; Hisn al-Muslim, no. 41

title: Prayer step: Sit up for a moment (Jalsah)
text:
Say “Allahu akbar” and sit up, resting your hands on your thighs. Sit still for a moment and ask for forgiveness.
Say: Allahu akbar — "Allah is the Greatest." [Said at each change of position]
Say: Rabbigh-fir lee, rabbigh-fir lee. — "My Lord, forgive me. My Lord, forgive me." [Hisn al-Muslim, no. 48]
Done differently: Most sit on the left foot with the right foot upright, toes towards the Qibla. If that hurts, sit however you comfortably can.
src: Said at each change of position; Hisn al-Muslim, no. 48

title: Prayer step: Prostrate a second time (Sujud)
text:
Say “Allahu akbar” and prostrate again, just like the first time. That completes one rakʿah.
Say: Allahu akbar — "Allah is the Greatest." [Said at each change of position]
Say: Subhana rabbiyal-aʿla — "How perfect my Lord is, the Most High." (3 times) [Hisn al-Muslim, no. 41]
src: Said at each change of position; Hisn al-Muslim, no. 41

title: Prayer step: Stand up for the next rakʿah (Qiyam)
text:
Say “Allahu akbar” and stand up again, hands folded as before. This rakʿah starts straight from al-Fatihah: no opening words this time.
Say: Allahu akbar — "Allah is the Greatest." [Said at each change of position]
src: Said at each change of position

title: Prayer step: Sit and bear witness (Tashahhud)
text:
After the second prostration of the second rakʿah, stay sitting instead of standing. With your hands on your thighs, recite the tashahhud. Many raise the right index finger when bearing witness.
Say: Attahiyyatu lillahi wassalawatu wattayyibat, assalamu ʿalayka ayyuhan-nabiyyu warahmatul-lahi wabarakatuh, assalamu ʿalayna waʿala ʿibadil-lahis-saliheen. Ash-hadu an la ilaha illal-lah, wa-ashhadu anna Muhammadan ʿabduhu warasooluh. — "All greetings of honour are for Allah, and all prayers and good things. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I bear witness that none has the right to be worshipped except Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger." [Hisn al-Muslim, no. 52]
Done differently: When and how the finger is raised, and the exact way of sitting, differ between schools. Ask your local imam.

title: Prayer step: Send blessings on the Prophet ﷺ (Salawat)
text:
In the final sitting only, after the tashahhud, send blessings on the Prophet ﷺ.
Say: Allahumma salli ʿala Muhammad, wa-ʿala ali Muhammad, kama sallayta ʿala Ibraheema wa-ʿala ali Ibraheem, innaka Hameedun Majeed. Allahumma barik ʿala Muhammad, wa-ʿala ali Muhammad, kama barakta ʿala Ibraheema wa-ʿala ali Ibraheem, innaka Hameedun Majeed. — "O Allah, send prayers upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You sent prayers upon Ibraheem and the family of Ibraheem; You are full of praise and majesty. O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibraheem and the family of Ibraheem; You are full of praise and majesty." [Hisn al-Muslim, no. 53]

title: Prayer step: Make a dua (Dua)
text:
Before ending the prayer you may ask Allah for anything good. This one was taught by the Prophet ﷺ. It is recommended, so leave it until you’re ready.
Say: Allahumma innee aʿoothu bika min ʿathabil-qabr, wamin ʿathabi jahannam, wamin fitnatil-mahya walmamat, wamin shari fitnatil-maseehid-dajjal. — "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave, from the punishment of Hell, from the trials of life and death, and from the evil of the trial of the False Messiah." [Hisn al-Muslim, no. 55]

title: Prayer step: End with peace (Taslim)
text:
Turn your head to the right and say the greeting of peace, then turn to the left and say it again. Your prayer is complete.
Say: As-salamu ʿalaykum wa rahmatullah — "Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah." (2 times) [Right, then left]

title: How to do wudu (washing before prayer)
text:
1. Intend and say Bismillah: Intend in your heart to make wudu for prayer, and say “Bismillah” (in the name of Allah).
2. Wash your hands ×3: Wash both hands up to the wrists, between the fingers too.
3. Rinse your mouth ×3: Take water into your mouth, swirl it around and spit it out.
4. Rinse your nose ×3: Sniff a little water into your nose with your right hand and blow it out with your left.
5. Wash your face ×3: From the hairline to the chin, and from ear to ear.
6. Wash your arms ×3: Right arm then left, from the fingertips up to and including the elbows.
7. Wipe your head: With wet hands, wipe over your head from the front to the back and back again.
8. Wipe your ears: With wet fingers, wipe inside your ears with your index fingers and behind them with your thumbs.
9. Wash your feet ×3: Right foot then left, up to and including the ankles, between the toes too.
10. Bear witness: Finish with the shahada.
Afterwards: Ashhadu an la ilaha illal-lahu wahdahu la shareeka lah, wa-ashhadu anna Muhammadan ʿabduhu warasooluh. — "I bear witness that none has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger."

title: Before you pray: Be clean
text: Make wudu (below). Your body, clothes and the place you pray should be clean; a prayer mat helps but isn’t required.

title: Before you pray: Cover yourself
text: Men cover at least from the navel to the knees, and usually the shoulders. Women cover everything except the face and hands; many also cover the feet. Loose clothes help.

title: Before you pray: Face the Qibla
text: Face the Kaaba in Makkah. Munib’s Qibla compass shows you which way.

title: Before you pray: Pray in its time
text: Each prayer has its own window during the day. Prayer times shows them for where you are.

title: Before you pray: For sisters
text: During a period, or bleeding after childbirth, a woman doesn’t pray, and doesn’t make up those prayers later. She can still remember Allah and make dua.

title: Before you pray: Start where you are
text: If you can’t say the Arabic yet, keep learning it and pray as well as you can; ask your local imam what to say until then. Allah doesn’t burden a soul beyond what it can bear (Quran 2:286).

title: The first word revealed was “Read”.
text: In the cave of Hira, near Makkah, the angel Jibril brought the first ayat: “Read in the name of your Lord who created.”

title: Al-Fatihah is recited at least 17 times a day.
text: It is part of every unit of prayer, and the five daily prayers have 17 units between them.

title: Ayat al-Kursi is the greatest ayah in the Quran.
text: The Prophet ﷺ asked Ubayy ibn Kaʿb which ayah was the greatest. He answered Ayat al-Kursi, and the Prophet ﷺ congratulated him on his knowledge.

title: Surah al-Ikhlas equals a third of the Quran.
text: Four short ayat about who Allah is. The Prophet ﷺ said reciting it is equal to reciting a third of the Quran.

title: Maryam is the only woman named in the Quran.
text: A whole surah, the nineteenth, carries her name.

title: The Quran was revealed a little at a time, over about 23 years.
text: Allah says He sent it down in parts “so you might recite it to the people slowly”. Small and steady was the way from the start.

title: Bismillah appears 114 times.
text: Surah at-Tawbah is the only surah that doesn’t open with it, and Surah an-Naml has it twice: once at the start, and once in Sulayman’s letter.

title: The longest ayah is about writing down a loan.
text: Ayah 282 of al-Baqarah tells believers to record debts in writing, with witnesses, so nobody is wronged.

title: Musa is named in the Quran more than any other prophet.
text: His story, from a baby in a basket on the river to standing before Pharaoh, is told across many surahs.

title: 25 prophets are named in the Quran.
text: From Adam to Muhammad ﷺ, including Ibrahim, Musa and ʿIsa. The Quran says there were others it does not name.

title: Allah is with you when you remember Him.
text: In a hadith qudsi, Allah says: “I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me.”

title: Saying of Ibn al-Qayyim (Scholar of 14th-century Damascus, known for his writing on the heart)
text: One of the signs of someone who truly knows Allah is that they don’t grieve over what they lose, nor become overly happy with what they gain. This is because they see everything as temporary and fading away, like shadows.

title: Saying of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (Closest companion of the Prophet ﷺ and the first caliph)
text: Whoever worshipped Muhammad, Muhammad has died. And whoever worships Allah, Allah is alive and never dies.
src: Sahih al-Bukhari 3668 (on the day the Prophet ﷺ died)

title: Saying of Umar ibn al-Khattab (Companion of the Prophet ﷺ and the second caliph)
text: Take account of yourselves before you are taken to account, and weigh your deeds before they are weighed for you.
src: Jamiʿ al-Tirmidhi, after 2459 · al-Zuhd of Imam Ahmad 633

title: Saying of Umar ibn al-Khattab (Companion of the Prophet ﷺ and the second caliph)
text: We were the most humbled of people, and Allah honoured us with Islam. If we ever seek honour in anything else, Allah will humble us.

title: Saying of Umar ibn al-Khattab (Companion of the Prophet ﷺ and the second caliph)
text: The best days we ever knew, we reached through patience. If patience were a man, he would be a noble one.
src: al-Sabr wal-Thawab of Ibn Abi al-Dunya, no. 6

title: Saying of Uthman ibn Affan (Companion of the Prophet ﷺ and the third caliph, who gathered the Quran into one book)
text: If our hearts were pure, they would never have enough of the speech of Allah.
src: Shuʿab al-Iman of al-Bayhaqi 2031 · Hilyat al-Awliya 7/272

title: Saying of Ali ibn Abi Talib (Cousin of the Prophet ﷺ and the fourth caliph)
text: This world is travelling away, and the Hereafter is travelling towards us, and each has its children. Be children of the Hereafter, not of this world. Today there is action and no reckoning; tomorrow there is reckoning and no action.
src: Sahih al-Bukhari, before 6417 (without a chain) · Musannaf Ibn Abi Shaybah 35636

title: Saying of Ali ibn Abi Talib (Cousin of the Prophet ﷺ and the fourth caliph)
text: Patience is to faith what the head is to the body. Cut off the head and the body dies. There is no faith for someone who has no patience.
src: al-Sabr wal-Thawab of Ibn Abi al-Dunya, no. 8

title: Saying of Abdullah ibn Masʿud (Companion of the Prophet ﷺ and one of the great teachers of the Quran)
text: This Quran is the banquet of Allah, so take from it what you can. A heart with nothing of the Book of Allah in it is like a ruined house that no one lives in.

title: Saying of Abdullah ibn Masʿud (Companion of the Prophet ﷺ and one of the great teachers of the Quran)
text: Don’t rush through it like poetry or scatter it like dry dates. Stop at its wonders and let it move your heart. Don’t let your only concern be reaching the end of the surah.

title: Saying of Abu al-Darda (Companion of the Prophet ﷺ, remembered for his wisdom and worship)
text: Everything has a polish, and the polish of the heart is the remembrance of Allah.

title: Saying of Abu al-Darda (Companion of the Prophet ﷺ, remembered for his wisdom and worship)
text: The peak of faith is four things: patience with the judgement of Allah, contentment with His decree, sincere trust in Him, and surrender to your Lord.
src: Sharh Usul Iʿtiqad Ahl al-Sunnah of al-Lalakaʾi, no. 1697

title: Saying of Umm al-Darda (Wife of Abu al-Darda, a scholar of the generation after the Companions)
text: Someone asked her which act of worship Abu al-Darda did most. She said: “Reflection, and taking lessons.”
src: al-Zuhd of Ibn al-Mubarak (riwayah of al-Marwazi), no. 286

title: Saying of al-Hasan al-Basri (Scholar and preacher of 1st-century Basra, from the generation after the Companions)
text: Son of Adam, you are nothing but a number of days. Whenever a day goes, a part of you goes with it.
src: Hilyat al-Awliya 2/148 · al-Zuhd of Imam Ahmad 1586

title: Saying of al-Fudayl ibn ʿIyad (Scholar of 2nd-century Makkah, who turned to Allah after a life of highway robbery)
text: A deed is only accepted when it is sincere and correct. Sincere means it is for Allah alone. Correct means it follows the Sunnah.
src: Iʿlam al-Muwaqqiʿin of Ibn al-Qayyim 3/124, on Quran 18:110

title: Saying of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz (Caliph of the 1st century, remembered for his justice)
text: Take care of your Hereafter, and Allah will take care of your life in this world. Take care of your private life, and Allah will take care of your public life.
src: al-Ikhlas wal-Niyyah of Ibn Abi al-Dunya, no. 50

title: Saying of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz (Caliph of the 1st century, remembered for his justice)
text: Thinking about the blessings of Allah is one of the best acts of worship.

title: Saying of Ibn al-Qayyim (Scholar of 14th-century Damascus, known for his writing on the heart)
text: In the heart there is an emptiness that nothing can fill except loving Allah, turning to Him, remembering Him always and being sincere to Him.

title: Saying of Ibn al-Qayyim (Scholar of 14th-century Damascus, known for his writing on the heart)
text: If you want to benefit from the Quran, gather your heart when you recite it and listen closely, as someone would who is being spoken to by Allah Himself.

title: Myth: You need to know Arabic before the Quran is for you.
text: The Prophet ﷺ said that someone who reads the Quran and finds it hard gets two rewards.

title: Myth: “Allah” is a different God from the God of Jews and Christians.
text: Allah is the Arabic word for God, and Arabic-speaking Christians say it too. The Quran says: “Our God and your God is one.”

title: Myth: The Quran was written down centuries after the Prophet ﷺ.
text: It was gathered into one book within about two years of his passing, under Abu Bakr. Copies were sent across the Muslim lands under ʿUthman, less than twenty years later.

title: Myth: Muslims worship the Kaaba.
text: Muslims face the Kaaba so they all pray in one direction, but they worship Allah alone. ʿUmar told the Black Stone: “I know that you are a stone that can neither harm nor benefit.”

title: Myth: People are forced to become Muslim.
text: The Quran says: “There shall be no compulsion in religion.” Faith only counts when it is chosen.

title: Myth: Women had no place in Islamic scholarship.
text: ʿAisha, may Allah be pleased with her, narrated over two thousand hadith and taught leading scholars of her time.
src: Narrations collected in al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: Myth: Crying when you lose someone means your iman is weak.
text: The Prophet ﷺ wept when his son Ibrahim died and said: “The eyes shed tears and the heart grieves, but we say only what pleases our Lord.”

title: Myth: Some sins are too big for Allah to forgive.
text: “Do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins.” The door stays open for anyone who turns back to Him.

title: Myth: Seeing a doctor shows weak faith.
text: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Allah has not sent down a disease without sending down a cure for it.” Seeking treatment is part of trusting Him.

title: What does "sabr" mean?
text: patience. From a root meaning to hold firm: staying steady when you want to give up. “Indeed, Allah is with the patient.”

title: What does "tawakkul" mean?
text: trust in Allah. Doing your part, then leaving the outcome to Allah. “Whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him.”

title: What does "shukr" mean?
text: gratitude. “If you are grateful, I will surely increase you.”

title: What does "raḥmah" mean?
text: mercy. Ar-Raḥmān and ar-Raḥīm, in every Bismillah, come from the same root as raḥim, the word for a mother’s womb.

title: What does "qalb" mean?
text: heart. Its root means to turn over. The Prophet ﷺ often prayed: “O Turner of hearts, keep my heart firm on Your religion.”

title: What does "dhikr" mean?
text: remembrance. “Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah hearts are assured.”

title: What does "tawbah" mean?
text: turning back. Repentance in Arabic is literally a turning back to Allah. It is the same idea as Munib’s name: one who turns back to Him.

title: What does "sakīnah" mean?
text: tranquillity. “It is He who sent down tranquillity into the hearts of the believers.”

title: What does "mawaddah" mean?
text: affection. Allah describes marriage this way: “He placed between you affection and mercy.”

title: What does "birr" mean?
text: goodness, especially to parents. “Your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and to parents, good treatment.”

title: What does "iḥsān" mean?
text: excellence. The Prophet ﷺ described it as worshipping Allah as if you see Him, and knowing that He sees you.

title: Dua: When worry won’t leave you
text: Allāhumma innī aʿūdhu bika minal-hammi wal-ḥazan, wal-ʿajzi wal-kasal, wal-bukhli wal-jubn, wa ḍalaʿid-dayni wa ghalabatir-rijāl — "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from worry and grief, from helplessness and laziness, from miserliness and cowardice, from the burden of debt and from being overpowered by others."

title: Dua: The dua of Yunus, from inside the whale
text: Lā ilāha illā anta, subḥānaka, innī kuntu minaẓ-ẓālimīn — "There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers."

title: Dua: The best way to ask forgiveness
text: Allāhumma anta rabbī, lā ilāha illā ant. Khalaqtanī wa ana ʿabduk, wa ana ʿalā ʿahdika wa waʿdika mastaṭaʿt. Aʿūdhu bika min sharri mā ṣanaʿt. Abū’u laka bi niʿmatika ʿalayy, wa abū’u laka bi dhanbī, faghfir lī, fa innahu lā yaghfirudh-dhunūba illā ant — "O Allah, You are my Lord; there is no god but You. You created me and I am Your servant, and I keep Your covenant and promise as best I can. I seek refuge in You from the evil I have done. I acknowledge Your blessings upon me, and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me, for none forgives sins but You."

title: Dua: The dua the Prophet ﷺ made most often
text: Rabbanā ātinā fid-dunyā ḥasanatan wa fil-ākhirati ḥasanatan wa qinā ʿadhāban-nār — "Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire."

title: Dua: For learning
text: Rabbi zidnī ʿilmā — "My Lord, increase me in knowledge."

title: Dua: Before something hard
text: Rabbish-raḥ lī ṣadrī, wa yassir lī amrī, waḥlul ʿuqdatan min lisānī, yafqahū qawlī — "My Lord, expand for me my breast, and ease for me my task, and untie the knot from my tongue, that they may understand my speech. (Musa’s dua before facing Pharaoh.)"

title: Dua: For your parents
text: Rabbir-ḥamhumā kamā rabbayānī ṣaghīrā — "My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up when I was small."

title: Dua: For your spouse and children
text: Rabbanā hab lanā min azwājinā wa dhurriyyātinā qurrata aʿyunin wajʿalnā lil-muttaqīna imāmā — "Our Lord, grant us from among our spouses and offspring comfort to our eyes, and make us an example for the righteous."

title: Dua: Zakariyya’s dua for a child
text: Rabbi lā tadharnī fardan wa anta khayrul-wārithīn — "My Lord, do not leave me alone (with no heir), while You are the best of inheritors."

title: Dua: When you lose something
text: Innā lillāhi wa innā ilayhi rājiʿūn. Allāhumma’jurnī fī muṣībatī wa akhlif lī khayran minhā — "We belong to Allah and to Him we return. O Allah, reward me in my loss and replace it for me with something better."

title: Dua: For someone who is ill
text: Adh-hibil-ba’s, rabban-nās, ishfi wa antash-shāfī, lā shifā’a illā shifā’uk, shifā’an lā yughādiru saqamā — "Remove the harm, Lord of mankind, and heal, for You are the Healer. There is no healing but Your healing, a healing that leaves no illness behind."

title: Dua: When money is tight
text: Allāhummakfinī bi ḥalālika ʿan ḥarāmik, wa aghninī bi faḍlika ʿamman siwāk — "O Allah, let what is lawful be enough for me instead of what is unlawful, and by Your bounty make me need no one but You."

title: Dua: When you feel the anger rising
text: Aʿūdhu billāhi minash-shayṭānir-rajīm — "I seek refuge in Allah from Satan, the accursed. The Prophet ﷺ said that if an angry man said this, his anger would leave him."

title: Dua: To keep your heart steady
text: Yā muqallibal-qulūb, thabbit qalbī ʿalā dīnik — "O Turner of hearts, keep my heart firm on Your religion."

title: Dua: To be grateful
text: Rabbi awziʿnī an ashkura niʿmatakal-latī anʿamta ʿalayya wa ʿalā wālidayya wa an aʿmala ṣāliḥan tarḍāh — "My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favour which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and to do righteousness of which You approve."

title: Dua: When there’s bad feeling between people
text: Rabbanaghfir lanā wa li ikhwāninal-ladhīna sabaqūnā bil-īmān, wa lā tajʿal fī qulūbinā ghillan lil-ladhīna āmanū — "Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who came before us in faith, and put no resentment in our hearts toward those who have believed."

title: Name of Allah: Ar-Razzāq (The Provider)
text: “Indeed, it is Allah who is the continual Provider, the firm possessor of strength.”

title: Name of Allah: Al-Wadūd (The Loving)
text: “And He is the Forgiving, the Affectionate.” His love is not earned by being perfect.

title: Name of Allah: Al-Ghafūr (The Forgiving)
text: “Do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins.”

title: Name of Allah: Al-Qarīb (The Near)
text: “When My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near. I respond to the call of the caller when he calls upon Me.”

title: Name of Allah: Al-Wakīl (The One you can rely on)
text: “Sufficient for us is Allah, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.”

title: Name of Allah: Ash-Shāfī (The Healer)
text: The Prophet ﷺ prayed for the sick: “Heal, for You are the Healer. There is no healing but Your healing.”

title: Name of Allah: Al-Ḥalīm (The Forbearing)
text: He sees our mistakes and does not rush to punish. “And Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.”

title: Name of Allah: Al-Hādī (The Guide)
text: “But sufficient is your Lord as a guide and a helper.”

title: Name of Allah: As-Salām (The Source of Peace)
text: One of the names in the last ayat of al-Hashr: “the Sovereign, the Pure, the Perfection (as-Salām)…”

title: Name of Allah: Ash-Shakūr (The Appreciative)
text: He rewards even small good deeds generously. “Indeed, He is Forgiving and Appreciative.”

title: Name of Allah: Al-Laṭīf (The Subtle, the Gentle)
text: He takes care of His servants in ways they don’t always see. “Allah is Subtle with His servants.”

title: Name of Allah: Ar-Raḥmān (The Most Merciful)
text: The name you say in every Bismillah. Every surah but one opens with His mercy.

title: After your next prayer, say SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah and Allahu Akbar 33 times each.
text: The Prophet ﷺ taught this to the poor of Madinah, who felt they couldn’t match the charity of the rich.

title: Smile at someone today.
text: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Your smiling in the face of your brother is charity.”

title: Say Bismillah before you eat, and eat with your right hand.
text: The Prophet ﷺ taught this to a boy at his table: “Mention the name of Allah, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is in front of you.”

title: Say salam to someone you don’t know.
text: Asked what in Islam is best, the Prophet ﷺ said: to feed people, and to greet those you know and those you don’t.

title: Move something out of someone’s way.
text: The Prophet ﷺ said removing something harmful from the road is a branch of faith.

title: Make dua for someone without telling them.
text: The Prophet ﷺ said an angel replies: “And for you the same.”

title: Call a relative you haven’t spoken to in a while.
text: The Prophet ﷺ said whoever wants their provision increased and their life extended should keep ties with their relatives.

title: Make wudu before you sleep tonight.
text: The Prophet ﷺ told a companion: when you go to bed, make wudu as you would for prayer.

title: If you get angry while standing, sit down.
text: The Prophet ﷺ said: if anger passes, good; if not, lie down.

title: Visit or message someone who is unwell.
text: The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever visits a sick person is in the harvest of Paradise until he returns.

title: Which surah doesn’t begin with Bismillah?
text: At-Tawbah. Surah at-Tawbah, the ninth surah, is the only one without it.

title: How many surahs are in the Quran?
text: 114. 114 surahs, from al-Fatihah to an-Nas.

title: Which surah did the Prophet ﷺ say equals a third of the Quran?
text: Al-Ikhlas. Surah al-Ikhlas: four ayat about who Allah is.

title: What was the first word revealed?
text: Iqraʾ (“Read”). “Read in the name of your Lord who created.” Revealed in the cave of Hira.

title: Which woman has a surah named after her?
text: Maryam. Surah Maryam, the nineteenth surah. She is the only woman named in the Quran.

title: Which is the longest surah?
text: Al-Baqarah. Al-Baqarah, with 286 ayat.

title: Which prophet called out to Allah from inside a whale?
text: Yunus. Yunus: “There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers.”

title: Which is the greatest ayah in the Quran?
text: Ayat al-Kursi. Ayat al-Kursi (2:255), as Ubayy ibn Kaʿb answered and the Prophet ﷺ confirmed.

title: Which surah is recited in every unit of prayer?
text: Al-Fatihah. The Prophet ﷺ said there is no prayer without al-Fatihah.

title: Near which city did the revelation begin?
text: Makkah. In the cave of Hira, on a mountain near Makkah.

title: The story of Yunus (part 1)
text: Yunus left his people in anger, before Allah allowed him to, and boarded a crowded ship.

title: The story of Yunus (part 2)
text: Swallowed by a whale, in darkness upon darkness, he called out: “There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers.”

title: The story of Yunus (part 3)
text: “So We responded to him and saved him from the distress. And thus do We save the believers.” No darkness is too deep to call out from.

title: The story of Yusuf (part 1)
text: Yusuf’s brothers were jealous of their father’s love for him. They threw him into the bottom of a well.

title: The story of Yusuf (part 2)
text: Sold as a slave, falsely accused and jailed for years, he stayed patient and kept his faith.

title: The story of Yusuf (part 3)
text: Years later, as a minister of Egypt, he met his brothers again and said: “No blame will there be upon you today. Allah will forgive you.”

title: The story of Ayyub (part 1)
text: Ayyub was tested with long illness and with the loss of his family.

title: The story of Ayyub (part 2)
text: He called to his Lord: “Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.”

title: The story of Ayyub (part 3)
text: Allah removed his hardship and gave him back his family and more. “Indeed, We found him patient, an excellent servant.”

title: The story of The mother of Musa (part 1)
text: Pharaoh was killing the newborn sons of the Children of Israel. Then Musa was born.

title: The story of The mother of Musa (part 2)
text: Allah inspired his mother: “When you fear for him, cast him into the river, and do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you.”

title: The story of The mother of Musa (part 3)
text: Pharaoh’s own household found the baby, and Musa was returned to his mother, “that she might be content and not grieve.”

title: The story of Ibrahim (part 1)
text: Ibrahim told his people their idols could neither hear nor help them, and broke them.

title: The story of Ibrahim (part 2)
text: They said: “Burn him and support your gods.” And they threw him into a fire.

title: The story of Ibrahim (part 3)
text: Allah said: “O fire, be coolness and safety upon Ibrahim.”

title: THE FIVE PILLARS OF ISLAM: Shahada · the declaration
text: “There is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.” Believing this and saying it is how a person becomes Muslim. It is the first of five pillars Islam is built on.

title: THE FIVE PILLARS OF ISLAM: Salah · prayer
text: Five prayers a day: Fajr at dawn, Dhuhr after midday, Asr in the afternoon, Maghrib at sunset and Isha at night. A few minutes each, facing the Kaaba in Makkah. “Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing.”

title: THE FIVE PILLARS OF ISLAM: Zakat · giving
text: Once a year, a Muslim with savings above a set minimum gives a small share, usually 2.5%, to people in need. Zakat means purification: “Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them.”

title: THE FIVE PILLARS OF ISLAM: Sawm · fasting
text: In Ramadan, Muslims fast from dawn until sunset: no food or drink, and extra care with words and deeds. “Fasting has been prescribed for you… that you may become mindful of Allah.”

title: THE FIVE PILLARS OF ISLAM: Hajj · pilgrimage
text: Once in a lifetime, for those who are able, Muslims travel to Makkah for Hajj, joining millions from every nation who stand together as equals before Allah.

title: THE SIX ARTICLES OF FAITH: Allah
text: Iman, faith, has six parts. The first is belief in Allah: one God, with no partner and nothing like Him. “Say, He is Allah, who is One.”

title: THE SIX ARTICLES OF FAITH: The angels
text: Angels are created by Allah from light, and they obey Him. Jibril is the angel who brought the Quran to the Prophet ﷺ.

title: THE SIX ARTICLES OF FAITH: The books
text: Allah sent revealed books: the Torah to Musa, the Psalms to Dawud, the Gospel to ʿIsa, and the Quran to Muhammad ﷺ, the last of them.

title: THE SIX ARTICLES OF FAITH: The messengers
text: Allah sent messengers to every nation, among them Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa and ʿIsa. Muslims believe in them all, and Muhammad ﷺ is the final one.

title: THE SIX ARTICLES OF FAITH: The Last Day
text: This life will end, and everyone will be brought back to account for what they did. “Whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it.”

title: THE SIX ARTICLES OF FAITH: Qadr · Allah’s decree
text: Nothing happens outside Allah’s knowledge and will, the easy and the hard. Knowing this is a comfort, “so that you not despair over what has eluded you, nor exult over what He has given you.”

title: THE LIFE OF THE PROPHET (part 1)
text: Muhammad ﷺ was born in Makkah around 570 CE. He lost his father before he was born and his mother as a young child, and grew up known as al-Amin, the trustworthy.

title: THE LIFE OF THE PROPHET (part 2)
text: At forty, in the cave of Hira, the angel Jibril brought him the first revelation: “Read in the name of your Lord who created.”

title: THE LIFE OF THE PROPHET (part 3)
text: For thirteen years he called the people of Makkah to worship Allah alone. Many believed, and many of them were persecuted for it.

title: THE LIFE OF THE PROPHET (part 4)
text: In 622 CE he migrated to Madinah. This journey, the Hijrah, is where the Islamic calendar begins.

title: THE LIFE OF THE PROPHET (part 5)
text: He returned to Makkah in peace, forgave those who had fought him, and passed away in Madinah in 632 CE, aged 63. Allah calls him “a mercy to the worlds.”

title: YOUR FIRST STEPS: Wudu · washing for prayer
text: Before praying, Muslims wash in a set way called wudu: hands, mouth and nose, face, arms to the elbows, wiping the head, then the feet. The Quran describes its heart.

title: YOUR FIRST STEPS: Salah · how prayer looks
text: Prayer is standing, bowing, prostrating and sitting, while reciting al-Fatihah and remembering Allah. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Pray as you have seen me pray.”

title: YOUR FIRST STEPS: Learn it with others
text: Nobody learns this from a card. Your local mosque will be glad to show you, step by step. Take it one prayer at a time: “Make things easy, and do not make them difficult.”

title: Becoming Muslim wipes the slate clean.
text: ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs was worried about his past when he accepted Islam. The Prophet ﷺ told him: “Do you not know that Islam wipes out what came before it?”

title: Even the Quran began gently.
text: ʿAisha explained that the first surahs spoke of Paradise and the Fire. Rules came later, once hearts were settled: “If the first thing revealed had been ‘Do not drink alcohol’, they would have said ‘We will never give it up.’”

title: The religion is easy.
text: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The religion is easy… so do what is right, get as close to it as you can, and be glad.”

title: You won’t be asked for more than you can carry.
text: “Allah does not charge a soul except with that within its capacity.”

title: What does "āyah" mean?
text: a verse; literally, a sign. The Quran has 6,236 ayat. The same word is used for Allah’s signs in nature: “Of His signs are the night and the day, and the sun and the moon.”

title: What does "sūrah" mean?
text: a chapter. The Quran has 114 surahs, from al-Fatihah, the Opening, to an-Nas. The longest, al-Baqarah, has 286 ayat; the shortest, al-Kawthar, has three.

title: What does "ḥadīth" mean?
text: a report. A record of what the Prophet ﷺ said, did or approved, passed on through a chain of named narrators. Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim gather the most reliable.
src: The collections of al-Bukhari and Muslim

title: What does "sunnah" mean?
text: the way. The Prophet’s ﷺ way of living and worshipping, which Muslims follow. “There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent example.”

title: What does "ṣalāh" mean?
text: prayer. The five daily prayers. The Prophet ﷺ said prayer is the first deed a person will be asked about on the Day of Judgement.

title: What does "duʿāʾ" mean?
text: calling on Allah. Any personal prayer, in any language, at any time. “Call upon Me; I will respond to you.”

title: What does "dīn" mean?
text: a way of life. Usually translated as religion, but it means a whole way of living. “This day I have perfected for you your deen.”

title: What does "īmān" mean?
text: faith. Belief in the heart, shown in words and actions. Its six parts are belief in Allah, the angels, the books, the messengers, the Last Day and qadr.

title: What does "tawḥīd" mean?
text: oneness. Believing that Allah is One, with no partner: the heart of Islam. “Say, He is Allah, who is One.”

title: What does "ummah" mean?
text: community. The worldwide family of Muslims, from every nation and colour. “You are the best community brought forth for mankind.”

title: What does "ḥalāl" mean?
text: permitted. Anything Allah allows, from food to work. Its opposite is ḥarām, forbidden. “Eat of what is lawful and good on the earth.”

title: What does "in shāʾ Allāh" mean?
text: if Allah wills. Said about anything you plan to do. “Never say of anything, ‘I will do that tomorrow,’ except ‘if Allah wills.’”

title: What does "mā shāʾ Allāh" mean?
text: what Allah has willed. Said when you admire something, remembering that it came from Him.

title: What does "al-ḥamdu lillāh" mean?
text: all praise is for Allah. The first words of al-Fatihah after the Bismillah, and a Muslim’s thanks for anything good. The Prophet ﷺ said it fills the scale.

title: What does "jazāk Allāhu khayran" mean?
text: may Allah reward you with good. A Muslim’s thank you. The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever says it to someone who did them a favour has praised them as fully as they can.

title: Myth: Most Muslims are Arab.
text: Only around one in five Muslims is Arab, and the country with the most Muslims is Indonesia. “We made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another.”

title: Myth: Muslims don’t believe in Jesus.
text: ʿIsa (Jesus) is one of the greatest prophets in Islam, and Muslims believe in his miraculous birth to Maryam. The Quran tells his story with deep respect.

title: Myth: You have to be a perfect Muslim before you start.
text: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Every child of Adam makes mistakes, and the best of those who make mistakes are those who repent.”

title: Duas: Words of remembrance for morning and evening
text:
— "Allah - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except for what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most High, the Most Great."
Then recite [Soorah al-Ikhlaas (112)], [Soorah al-Falaq (113)] and [Soorah an-Naas (114)] — "([Soorah al-Ikhlaas (112)]( 1 ) Say, He is Allah, [who is] One,( 2 ) Allah, the Eternal Refuge.( 3 ) He neither begets nor is born,( 4 ) Nor is there to Him any equivalent.)([Soorah al-Falaq (113)] ( 1 ) Say, I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak( 2 ) From the evil of that which He created( 3 ) And from the evil of darkness when it settles( 4 ) And from the evil of the blowers in knots( 5 ) And from the evil of an envier when he envies. )([Soorah an-Naas (114)])( 1 ) Say, I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind,( 2 ) The Sovereign of mankind.( 3 ) The God of mankind,( 4 ) From the evil of the retreating whisperer -( 5 ) Who whispers [evil] into the breasts of mankind -( 6 ) From among the jinn and mankind." (3 times)
Asbahna wa-asbahal-mulku lillah walhamdu lillah la ilaha illal-lah, wahdahu la shareeka lah, lahul-mulku walahul-hamd, wahuwa ʿala kulli shayin qadeer, rabbi as-aluka khayra ma fee hathihil-laylah, wakhayra ma baʿdaha, wa-aʿoothu bika min sharri hathihil-laylah, washarri ma baʿdaha, rabbi aʿoothu bika minal-kasal, wasoo-il kibar, rabbi aʿoothu bika min ʿathabin fin-nar, waʿathabin fil-qabr.‘We have reached the morning and at this very time unto Allah belongs all sovereignty, and all praise is for Allah. None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone, without partner, to Him belongs all sovereignty and praise and He is over all things omnipotent. My Lord, I ask You for the good of this night and the good of what follows it and I take refuge in You from the evil of this night and the evil of what follows it. My Lord, I take refuge in You from laziness and senility. My Lord, I take refuge in You from torment in the Fire and punishment in the grave.’…likewise, one says in the morning:Amsayna wa-amsal-mulku lillah….‘We have reached the evening and at this very time unto Allah belongs all sovereignty…’ — "‘We have reached the morning and at this very time unto Allaah, belongs all sovereignty , and all praise is for Allaah. None has the right to be worshipped except Allaah, alone, without any partner, to Him belong all sovereignty and praise and He is over all things omnipotent. My Lord, I ask You for the good of this day and the good of what follows it and I take refuge in You from the evil of this day and the evil of what follows it . My Lord, I take refuge in You from laziness and senility. My Lord, I take refuge in You from torment in the Fire and punishment in the grave.’"
(Allahumma bika asbahna wabika amsayna, wabika nahya ,wabika namootu wa-ilaykan-nushoor.)[In the evening:] (Allahumma bika amsayna, wabika asbahna, wabika nahya wabika namootu wa-ilaykal-maseer.) — "(O Allah, by your leave we have reached the morning and by Your leave we have reached the evening, by Your leave we live and die and unto You is our resurrection.)[In the evening:](O Allah, by Your leave we have reached the evening and by Your leave we have reached the morning, by Your leave we live and die and unto You is our return.)"
Allahumma anta rabbee la ilaha illa ant, khalaqtanee wa-ana ʿabduk, wa-ana ʿala ʿahdika wawaʿdika mas-tataʿt, aʿoothu bika min sharri ma sanaʿt, aboo-o laka biniʿmatika ʿalay, wa-aboo-o bithanbee, faghfir lee fa-innahu la yaghfiruth-thunooba illa ant. — "O Allah, You are my Lord, none has the right to be worshipped except You, You created me and I am Your servant and I abide to Your covenant and promise as best I can, I take refuge in You from the evil of which I have committed. I acknowledge Your favour upon me and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me, for verily none can forgive sin except You."
(Allahumma innee asbahtu oshhiduk, wa-oshhidu hamalata ʿarshik, wamala-ikatak, wajameeʿa khalqik, annaka antal-lahu la ilaha illa ant, wahdaka la shareeka lak, wa-anna Muhammadan ʿabduka warasooluk .) (four times in the morning & evening)(Note: for the evening, one reads (amsaytu) instead of (asbahtu).) — "(O Allah, verily I have reached the morning and call on You, the bearers of Your throne, Your angles, and all of Your creation to witness that You are Allah, none has the right to be worshipped except You, alone, without partner and that Muhammad is Your Servant and Messenger.) (four times in the morning & evening)(Note: for the evening, one reads (amsaytu) instead of (asbahtu).)" (4 times)
(Allahumma ma asbaha bee min niʿmatin, aw bi-ahadin min khalqik, faminka wahdaka la shareeka lak, falakal-hamdu walakash-shukr.)(Note: for the evening, one reads (amsa) instead of (asbaha).) — "(O Allah, what blessing I or any of Your creation have risen upon, is from You alone, without partner, so for You is all praise and unto You all thanks.)(…whoever says this in the morning has indeed offered his day’s thanks and whoever says this in the evening has indeed offered his night’s thanks.)(Note: for the evening, one reads (amsa) instead of (asbaha).)"
(Allahumma ʿafinee fee badanee, allahumma ʿafinee fee samʿee, allahumma ʿafinee fee basaree, la ilaha illa ant.(three times).)(Allahumma innee aʿoothu bika minal-kufr, walfaqr, wa-aʿoothu bika min ʿathabil-qabr, la ilaha illa ant (three times).) — "(O Allah, grant my body health, O Allah, grant my hearing health, O Allah, grant my sight health. None has the right to be worshipped except You.)(three times) (O Allah, I take refuge with You from disbelief and poverty, and I take refuge with You from the punishment of the grave. None has the right to be worshipped except You. (three times))" (3 times)
(Hasbiyal-lahu la ilaha illa huwa, ʿalayhi tawakkalt, wahuwa rabbul-ʿarshil-ʿatheem (Recite seven times in Arabic.) — "Allah is Sufficient for me, none has the right to be worshipped except Him, upon Him I rely and He is Lord of the exalted throne.’ (Recite seven times in Arabic.)"
Allahumma innee as-alukal-ʿafwa walʿafiyah, fid-dunya wal-akhirah, allahumma innee as-alukal-ʿafwa walʿafiyah fee deenee, wadunyaya wa-ahlee, wamalee, allahummas-tur ʿawratee, wa-amin rawʿatee, allahummah-fathnee min bayni yaday, wamin khalfee, waʿan yameenee, waʿan shimalee, wamin fawqee, wa-aʿoothu biʿathamatika an oghtala min tahtee. — "O Allah, I ask You for pardon and well-being in this life and the next. O Allah, I ask You for pardon and well-being in my religious and worldly affairs, and my family and my wealth. O Allah, veil my weaknesses and set at ease my dismay. O Allah, preserve me from the front and from behind and on my right and on my left and from above, and I take refuge with You lest I be swallowed up by the earth."
Allahumma ʿalimal-ghaybi washshahadah, fatiras-samawati wal-ard, rabba kulli shayin wamaleekah, ashhadu an la ilaha illa ant, aʿoothu bika min sharri nafsee wamin sharrish-shaytani washirkih, waan aqtarifa ʿala nafsee soo-an aw ajurrahu ila muslim. — "(O Allah, Knower of the unseen and the seen, Creator of the heavens and the Earth, Lord and Sovereign of all things, I bear witness that none has the right to be worshipped except You. I take refuge in You from the evil of my soul and from the evil and shirk of the devil, and from committing wrong against my soul or bringing such upon another Muslim.)(shirk: to associate others with Allah in those things which are specific to Him. This can occur in (1) belief, e.g. to believe that other than Allah has the power to benefit or harm, (2) speech, e.g. to swear by other than Allah and (3) action, e.g. to bow or prostrate to other than Allah.)"
Bismil-lahil-lathee la yadurru maʿas-mihi shay-on fil-ardi wala fis-sama-i wahuwas-sameeʿul-ʿaleem. (three times). — "In the name of Allah with whose name nothing is harmed on earth nor in the heavens and He is The All-Seeing, The All-Knowing.’(three times)" (3 times)
Radeetu billahi rabban wabil-islami deenan wabiMuhammadin nabiyya. (three times) — "I am pleased with Allah as a Lord, and Islam as a religion and Muhammad as a Prophet.’(three times)" (3 times)
Ya hayyu ya qayyoom, birahmatika astagheeth, aslih lee shaʾnee kullah, wala takilnee ila nafsee tarfata ʿayn. — "O Ever Living, O Self-Subsisting and Supporter of all, by Your mercy I seek assistance, rectify for me all of my affairs and do not leave me to myself, even for the blink of an eye."
(Asbahna wa-asbahal-mulku lillahi rabbil-ʿalameen, allahumma innee as-aluka khayra hathal-yawm, fat-hahu, wanasrahu, wanoorahu, wabarakatahu, wahudahu, wa-aʿoothu bika min sharri ma feehi, washarri ma baʿdah.)[For the evening, the supplication is read as follows: ](Amsayna wa-amsal-mulku lillahi rabbil-ʿalameen, allahumma innee as-aluka khayra hathihil-laylah, fat-haha, wanasraha, wanooraha, wabarakataha, wahudaha, wa-aʿoothu bika min sharri ma feeha washarri ma baʿdaha.) — "(We have reached the morning and at this very time all sovereignty belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds. O Allah, I ask You for the good of this day, its triumphs and its victories, its light and its blessings and its guidance, and I take refuge in You from the evil of this day and the evil that follows it.)[For the evening, the supplication is read as follows:](We have reached the evening and at this very time all sovereignty belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds. O Allah, I ask You for the good of tonight, its triumphs and its victories, its light and its blessings and its guidance, and I take refuge in You from the evil of tonight and the evil that follows it.)"
(Asbahna ʿala fitratil-islam, waʿala kalimatil-ikhlas, waʿala deeni nabiyyina Muhammad waʿala millati abeena Ibraheem, haneefan musliman wama kana minal-mushrikeen.)(Note: for the evening, one reads amsayna instead of asbahna.) — "(We rise upon the fitrah of Islam, and the word of pure faith, and upon the religion of our Prophet Muhammad and the religion of our forefather Ibraheem, who was a Muslim and of true faith and was not of those who associate others with Allah.)(fitrah: the religion of Islam, the way of Ibraheem u.)(Note: for the evening, one reads amsayna instead of asbahna.)"
(Subhanal-lahi wabihamdih.)one hundred times) — "(How perfect Allah is and I praise Him.)(one hundred times)" (100 times)
La ilaha illal-lah, wahdahu la shareeka lah, lahul-mulku walahul-hamd, wahuwa ʿala kulli shay-in qadeer. [ten times or once if lazy] — "(None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone, without partner, to Him belongs all sovereignty and praise, and He is over all things omnipotent.)( [ten times or once if lazy])" (10 times)
La ilaha illal-lah, wahdahu la shareeka lah, lahul-mulku walahul-hamd, wahuwa ʿala kulli shay-in qadeer. (one hundred times every day) — "(None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone, without partner, to Him belongs all sovereignty and praise, and He is over all things omnipotent.)((one hundred times every day))" (100 times)
(Subhanal-lahi wabihamdih, ʿadada khalqihi warida nafsih, wazinata ʿarshih, wamidada kalimatih.)(three times) — "(How perfect Allah is and I praise Him by the number of His creation and His pleasure, and by the weight of His throne, and the ink of His words.)(three times)" (3 times)
Allahumma innee as-aluka ʿilman nafiʿan, warizqan tayyiban, waʿamalan mutaqabbalan. — "O Allah, I ask You for knowledge which is beneficial and sustenance which is good, and deeds which are acceptable."
Astaghfirullaaha wa 'atoobu 'ilayhi[one hundred times a day] — "‘I seek Allaah’s forgiveness and I turn to Him in repentance.’ [one hundred times a day]" (100 times)
(aʿoothu bikalimatil-lahit-tammati min sharri ma khalaq.) (three times in the evening) — "(I take refuge in Allah’s perfect words from the evil He has created.)(three times in the evening)" (3 times)
Allaahumma salli wa sallim 'alaa Nabiyyinaa Muhammadin[ten times] — "‘O Allaah, send prayers and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad.’ [ten times]" (10 times)

title: Duas: What to say before sleeping
text:
— "When retiring to his bed every night, the Prophet would hold his palms together, spit (A form of spitting comprising mainly of air with little spittle) in them, recite the last three chapters (Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq, An-Nas) of the Quran and then wipe over his entire body as much as possible with his hands, beginning with his head and face and then all parts of the body, he would do this three times." (3 times)
 — "Allah - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except for what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most High, the Most Great."
 — "( 285 ) The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and [so have] the believers. All of them have believed in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers, [saying], We make no distinction between any of His messengers. And they say, We hear and we obey. [We seek] Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the [final] destination.( 286 ) Allah does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. It will have [the consequence of] what [good] it has gained, and it will bear [the consequence of] what [evil] it has earned. Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we have forgotten or erred. Our Lord, and lay not upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear. And pardon us; and forgive us; and have mercy upon us. You are our protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people."
Bismika rabbee wadaʿtu janbee wabika arfaʿuh, fa-in amsakta nafsee farhamha, wa-in arsaltaha fahfathha bima tahfathu bihi ʿibadakas-saliheen. — "In Your name my Lord, I lie down and in Your name I rise, so if You should take my soul then have mercy upon it, and if You should return my soul then protect it in the manner You do so with Your righteous servants."
Allahumma innaka khalaqta nafsee wa-anta tawaffaha, laka mamatuha wamahyaha in ahyaytaha fahfathha, wa-in amattaha faghfir laha. Allahumma innee as-alukal-ʿafiyah. — "O Allah, verily You have created my soul and You shall take it’s life, to You belongs it’s life and death. If You should keep my soul alive then protect it, and if You should take it’s life then forgive it. O Allah, I ask You to grant me good health."
Allahumma qinee ʿathabaka yawma tabʿathu ʿibadak. — "O Allah, protect me from Your punishment on the day Your servants are resurrected."
Bismikal-lahumma amootu wa-ahya. — "In Your name O Allah, I live and die."
Subhanal-lah. (thirty-three times) Alhamdu lillah. (thirty-three times) Allahu akbar. (thirty-four times) — "How Perfect Allah is. (thirty-three times) All praise is for Allah.(thirty-three times) Allah is the greatest.(thirty-four times)"
Allahumma rabbas-samawatis-sabʿ, warabbal-ʿarshil-ʿatheem, rabbana warabba kulli shayʾ, faliqal-habbi wannawa, wamunazzilat-tawra, wal-injeel, walfurqan, aʿoothu bika min sharri kulli shayin anta akhithun binasiyatih. Allahumma antal-awwal, falaysa qablaka shayʾ, wa-antal-akhir, falaysa baʿdaka shayʾ, wa-antath-thahir falaysa fawqaka shayʾ, waantal-batin, falaysa doonaka shayʾ, iqdi ʿannad-dayna wa-aghnina minal-faqr. — "(O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and the exalted throne, our Lord and Lord of all things, Splitter of the seed and the date stone, Revealer of the Tawrah, the Injeel and the Furqan, I take refuge in You from the evil of all things You shall seize by the forelock (i.e. You have total mastery over). O Allah, You are The First so there is nothing before You and You are The Last so there is nothing after You.You are Aththahir so there is nothing above You and You are Al-Batin so there is nothing closer than You.Settle our debt for us and spare us from poverty.)(Tawrah: The book revealed to Moosa u.)(Injeel: The book revealed to Easa u.)(Furqan: One of the many names of the Quran, means: The Criterion which distinguishes between truth and falsehood.)(Aththahir: Indicates the greatness of His attributes and the insignificance of every single creation in respect to His greatness and Highness, for He is above all of His creation as regards His essence and attributes.)(Al-Batin: Indicates His awareness and knowledge of all secrets, of that which is in the hearts and the most intimate of things just as it indicates His closeness and nearness to all in a manner which befits His majesty.)"
Alhamdu lillahil-lathee atʿamana wasaqana, wakafana, wa-awana, fakam mimman la kafiya lahu wala mu'wee. — "All praise is for Allah, Who fed us and gave us drink, and Who is sufficient for us and has sheltered us, for how many have none to suffice them or shelter them."
Allahumma ʿalimal-ghaybi washshahadah, fatiras-samawati wal-ard, rabba kulli shayin wamaleekah, ashhadu an la ilaha illa ant, aʿoothu bika min sharri nafsee wamin sharrish-shaytani washirkih, wa-an aqtarifa ʿala nafsee soo-an aw ajurrahu ila muslim. — "(O Allah, Knower of the seen and the unseen, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Lord and Sovereign of all things I bear witness that none has the right to be worshipped except You. I take refuge in You from the evil of my soul and from the evil and shirk of the devil, and from committing wrong against my soul or bringing such upon another Muslim.)(shirk: to associate others with Allah in those things which are specific to Him. This can occur in (1) belief, e.g. to believe that other than Allah has the power to benefit or harm, (2) speech, e.g. to swear by other than Allah and (3) action, e.g. to bow or prostrate to other than Allah.)"
 — "The Prophet never used to sleep until he had recited Soorat As-Sajdah (chapter 32) and Soorat Al-Mulk (chapter 67)."
Allahumma aslamtu nafsee ilayk, wafawwadtu amree ilayk, wawajjahtu wajhee ilayk, wa-aljaʾtu thahree ilayk, raghbatan warahbatan ilayk, la maljaa wala manja minka illa ilayk, amantu bikitabikal-lathee anzalt, wabinabiyyikal-lathee arsalt. — "(O Allah, I submit my soul unto You, and I entrust my affair unto You, and I turn my face towards You, and I totally rely on You, in hope and fear of You.Verily there is no refuge nor safe haven from You except with You. I believe in Your Book which You have revealed and in Your Prophet whom You have sent.)(If you then die, you will die upon the fitrah.)(fitrah: the religion of Islam, the way of Ibraheem u.)"

title: Duas: Supplications for when you wake up
text:
Alhamdu lillahil-lathee ahyana baʿda ma amatana wa-ilayhin-nushoor. — "All praise is for Allah who gave us life after having taken it from us and unto Him is the resurrection."
La ilaha illal-lahu wahdahu la shareeka lah, lahul-mulku walahul-hamd, wahuwa ʿala kulli shay-in qadeer, subhanal-lah, walhamdu lillah, wala ilaha illal-lah wallahu akbar, wala hawla wala quwwata illa billahil-ʿaliyyil ʿatheem. Rabbigh-fir lee — "None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone without associate, to Him belongs sovereignty and praise and He is over all things wholly capable. How perfect Allah is, and all praise is for Allah, and none has the right to be worshipped except Allah, Allah is the greatest and there is no power nor might except with Allah, The Most High, The Supreme.O my Lord forgive me"
Alhamdu lillahil-lathee ʿafanee fee jasadee waradda ʿalayya roohee wa-athina lee bithikrih. — "All praise is for Allah who restored to me my health and returned my soul and has allowed me to remember Him."
From Verse 3:190 till the end of the chapter Al-Imran — "( 190 ) Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding.( 191 ) Who remember Allah while standing or sitting or [lying] on their sides and give thought to the creation of the heavens and the earth, [saying], Our Lord, You did not create this aimlessly; exalted are You [above such a thing]; then protect us from the punishment of the Fire.( 192 ) Our Lord, indeed whoever You admit to the Fire - You have disgraced him, and for the wrongdoers there are no helpers.( 193 ) Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith, [saying], 'Believe in your Lord,' and we have believed. Our Lord, so forgive us our sins and remove from us our misdeeds and cause us to die with the righteous.( 194 ) Our Lord, and grant us what You promised us through Your messengers and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You do not fail in [Your] promise.( 195 ) And their Lord responded to them, Never will I allow to be lost the work of [any] worker among you, whether male or female; you are of one another. So those who emigrated or were evicted from their homes or were harmed in My cause or fought or were killed - I will surely remove from them their misdeeds, and I will surely admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow as reward from Allah, and Allah has with Him the best reward.( 196 ) Be not deceived by the [uninhibited] movement of the disbelievers throughout the land.( 197 ) [It is but] a small enjoyment; then their [final] refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place.( 198 ) But those who feared their Lord will have gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding eternally therein, as accommodation from Allah. And that which is with Allah is best for the righteous.( 199 ) And indeed, among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in Allah and what was revealed to you and what was revealed to them, [being] humbly submissive to Allah. They do not exchange the verses of Allah for a small price.Those will have their reward with their Lord. Indeed, Allah is swift in account.( 200 ) O you who have believed, persevere and endure and remain stationed and fear Allah that you may be successful."

title: Duas: Invocation for entering the restroom
text: (Bismil-lah) allahumma innee aʿoothu bika minal-khubthi wal-khaba-ith. — "(In the name of Allah). O Allah, I take refuge with you from all evil and evil-doers."

title: Duas: Invocation for leaving the restroom
text: Ghufranak. — "I ask You (Allah) for forgiveness."

title: Duas: What to say before performing ablution
text: Bismil-lah. — "In the name of Allah."

title: Duas: What to say upon completing ablution
text:
Ashhadu an la ilaha illal-lahu wahdahu la shareeka lah, wa-ashhadu anna Muhammadan ʿabduhu warasooluh. — "I bear witness that none has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His slave and Messenger."
Allahummaj-ʿalnee minat-tawwabeena wajʿalnee minal-mutatahhireen. — "O Allah, make me of those who return to You often in repentance and make me of those who remain clean and pure."
Subhanakal-lahumma wabihamdika ashhadu an la ilaha illa anta astaghfiruka wa-atoobu ilayk. — "How perfect You are O Allah, and I praise You, I bear witness that none has the right to be worshipped except You, I seek Your forgiveness and turn in repentance to You."

title: Duas: What to say when leaving the home
text:
Bismil-lah, tawakkaltu ʿalal-lah, wala hawla wala quwwata illa billah. — "In the name of Allah, I place my trust in Allah, and there is no might nor power except with Allah."
Allahumma innee aʿoothu bika an adilla aw odal, aw azilla aw ozall, aw athlima aw othlam, aw ajhala aw yujhala ʿalay. — "(O Allah, I take refuge with You lest I should stray or be led astray, or slip or be tripped, or oppress or be oppressed, or behave foolishly or be treated foolishly.)(slip: i.e. to commit a sin unintentionally)"

title: Duas: What to say when entering the home
text: Bismil-lahi walajna, wabismil-lahi kharajna, waʿala rabbina tawakkalna. — "In the name of Allah we enter and in the name of Allah we leave, and upon our Lord we place our trust."

title: Duas: Invocation for going to the mosque
text: Allaahummaj 'al fee qalbee nooran, wa fee lisaanee nooran, wa fee sam'ee nooran, wa fee basaree nooran, wa min fawqee nooran, wa min tahtee nooran, wa 'an yameenee nooran, wa 'an shimaalee nooran, wa min 'amaamee nooran, wa min khalfee nooran. Wa j'al fee nafsee nooran, wa 'a'dhim lee nooran, wa 'a'dhim lee nooran. Waj'al lee nooran, waj'alnee nooran. Allaahumma a'tineje nooran, waj'al fee 'asabee nooran, wa fee lahmee nooran, wa fee damee nooran, wa fee sha'ree nooran, wa fee basharee nooran.[Allaahummaj'al lee nooran fee qabree, wa nooran fee 'idhaamee.][Wa zidnee nooran, wa zidnee nooran, wa zidnee nooran.][Wa hab lee nooran 'alaa noor.] — "‘O Allaah, place within my heart light; and upon my tongue light; and within my ears light; and within my eyes light; and place above me light; and beneath me light; and on my right light; and on my left light; and in front of me light; and behind me light; and place light within my soul; and augment light for me; and greaten light for me; and grant me light and make me light. O Allaah, bestow upon me light; and place light in my tendons; and light in my flesh; and light in my blood; and in light in my hair and light in my skin.’ [O Allaah, place light for me in my grave and light in my bones]. [And increase me with light and increase me with light and increase me with light]. [And grant me light upon light.]’"

title: Duas: Invocation for entering the mosque
text: aʿoothu billahil-ʿatheem wabiwajhihil-kareem wasultanihil-qadeem minash-shaytanir-rajeem, [bismil-lah, wassalatu] [wassalamu ʿala rasoolil-lah] , allahumma iftah lee abwaba rahmatik. — "I take refuge with Allah, The Supreme and with His Noble Face, and His eternal authority from the accursed devil. In the name of Allah, and prayers and peace be upon the Messenger of Allah. O Allah, open the gates of Your mercy for me."

title: Duas: Invocation for leaving the mosque
text: Bismil-lah wassalatu wassalamu ʿala rasoolil-lah, allahumma innee as-aluka min fadlik, allahumma iʿsimnee minash-shaytanir-rajeem. — "In the name of Allah, and prayers and peace be upon the Messenger of Allah. O Allah, I ask You from Your favour. O Allah, guard me from the accursed devil."

title: Duas: What to say upon hearing the Athan (call to prayer)
text:
— "‘One repeats just as the mu-aththin (one who calls to prayer) says, except when he says: Hayya AAalas-salah (or) hayya AAalal-falah ‘come to prayer, come to success’ instead, one should say: La hawla wala quwwata illa billah. ‘There is no might nor power except with Allah.’"
Immediately following the declaration of faith called by the mu-aththin, one says:Wa-ana ashhadu an la ilaha illal-lahu wahdahu la shareeka lah, wa-anna Muhammadan ʿabduhu warasooluh, radeetu billahi rabban wabimuhammadin rasoolan wabil-islami deena. — "Immediately following the declaration of faith called by the mu-aththin, one says:‘And I too bear witness that none has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone, without partner, and that Muhammad is His salve and Messenger. I am pleased with Allah as a Lord, and Muhammad as a Messenger and Islam as a religion.’"
 — "‘One should then send prayers on the Prophet (sal-Allaahu 'alayhe wa sallam) after answering the call of the mu.adhdhin’."
Allahumma rabba hathihid-daʿwatit-tammah, wassalatil-qa-imah ati Muhammadan alwaseelata wal-fadeelah, wabʿath-hu maqaman mahmoodan allathee waʿadtah, innaka la tukhliful-meeʿad. — "‘O Allah, Owner of this perfect call and Owner of this prayer to be performed, bestow upon Muhammad al-waseelah and al-fadeelah and send him upon a praised platform which You have promised him. Verily, You never fail in Your promise.’al-waseelah: A station in paradise.al-fadeelah: A rank above the rest of creation.praised platform: One in which all of creation will praise him on, in order to bring about the account quickly and be relieved from the lengthy standing or the role of intercession."
 — "One should also supplicate for himself during the time between the athan and the iqamah as supplication at such time is not rejected."

title: Duas: Invocation when getting dressed
text: Alhamdu lillahil-lathee kasanee hatha (aththawb) warazaqaneehi min ghayri hawlin minnee wala quwwah. — "All Praise is for Allah who has clothed me with this garment and provided it for me, with no power nor might from myself."

title: Duas: Invocation when putting on new clothes
text: Allahumma lakal-hamdu anta kasawtaneeh, as-aluka min khayrihi wakhayri ma suniʿa lah, wa-aʿoothu bika min sharrihi washarri ma suniʿa lah. — "O Allah, for You is all praise, You have clothed me with it (i.e. the garment), I ask You for the good of it and the good for which it was made, and I seek refuge with You from the evil of it and the evil for which it was made."
